observations.text: SP entered and maintained the holding pattern to the level required for this stage; however, the entry type was determined only after the IP identified the entry sector, and the drift correction on the outbound leg was applied on the IP's direction. Deviation from the holding pattern reached 11 degrees and the inbound leg was flown 25 knots off the holding speed before the IP took part in the correction. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent determination of the entry and of the drift correction is expected to improve on the following sorties.

SP, working from the holding procedures of the Techniques and Procedures Manual and AFMAN 11-202 VOL3, determined the entry sector and flew the teardrop entry without the IP having to direct it. Correction for the wind change on the outbound leg was applied after two verbal prompts from the IP, with the deviation from the holding pattern at 8 degrees and the airspeed 20 knots off the holding speed. Errors were recognized and corrected, although with delay. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP identified the entry sector before reaching the fix and entered the pattern without IP intervention, complying with the ATC holding clearance as issued. Minor errors in the drift correction on the outbound leg produced a deviation of 7 degrees from the holding pattern and 15 knots on the holding speed, which the SP recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Pre-descent checks were executed inside the pattern with no assistance required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP determined the entry accurately and quickly and established the aircraft on the holding radial immediately after crossing the fix. Wind changes at the holding altitude were compensated without the IP's intervention, keeping the deviation from the holding pattern inside 4 degrees, the airspeed within 8 knots of the holding speed and the crossing of the IAF within 1 minute of the estimate passed to ATC. Pre-descent checks were executed inside the pattern without prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP applied the standardized holding procedure flawlessly, selecting the entry before reaching the fix and cross-checking the pattern against the raw radial and DME picture. Drift correction was anticipatory on every leg, so that the deviation from the holding pattern remained within 2 degrees, the airspeed within 3 knots of the holding speed and the crossing of the IAF within 15 seconds of the estimate. The aircraft remained well inside the protected holding airspace and all ATC instructions were complied with as issued. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized method of determining the entry sector, did not orient the holding course against the aircraft heading before reaching the fix and flew a direct entry where a parallel entry was required. The error was not corrected on the first circuit, with the result that the deviation from the holding pattern exceeded 12 degrees, the aircraft reached the edge of the protected holding airspace and the IP had to direct the re-entry and fly part of the pattern. Further study of the holding entry procedures in the Techniques and Procedures Manual and AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 is required.

SP, due to lack of knowledge of the published procedure for the condition encountered, did not apply the holding speed prescribed for the assigned altitude and did not start the outbound timing at the abeam position. The airspeed diverged by 28 knots from the holding speed and the crossing of the IAF differed by 3 minutes from the estimate passed to ATC, with the result that the IP directed the corrections and flew part of the pattern. Study of the holding speeds and timing limits is required before the next sortie.

SP entered and maintained the holding pattern within the standards required for this stage; however, the correction of the outbound heading for drift and the adjustment of the outbound timing were made only after the IP's verbal prompts, and the deviations were recognized with delay. Deviation from the holding pattern reached 8 degrees and the airspeed 20 knots off the holding speed before the corrections took effect. Marginal performance for the Training Section - recognition of the wind effect without prompting is expected to improve.

SP determined the entry sector before reaching the fix and entered the pattern without IP direction, complying with the ATC holding clearance as issued. Minor errors in the outbound timing produced a crossing of the IAF 1.5 minutes off the estimate passed to ATC and a deviation of 6 degrees from the holding pattern, both of which the SP identified and corrected without the IP's intervention. Pre-descent checks were completed inside the pattern. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP determined the entry sector before reaching the fix and rolled out on the holding radial with the drift correction already applied. The pattern was flown accurately and quickly throughout, with the deviation from the holding pattern held inside 3 degrees and the airspeed within 7 knots of the holding speed, and with no assistance from the IP at any point. ATC holding instructions were read back and complied with as issued. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the holding pattern with exceptional accuracy, computing the entry and the drift correction from the winds before reaching the fix and refining the outbound timing on every circuit. Deviations were negligible, remaining within 1 degree of the holding pattern, within 4 knots of the holding speed and within 20 seconds of the estimated time over the IAF. Knowledge of the holding procedure and its application were above the levels desired for this stage of training. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized technique for timing the holding legs, did not start the outbound timing abeam the fix and did not adjust the outbound leg to produce a one minute inbound leg. The error was repeated on the second circuit, with the result that the crossing of the IAF differed by 3 minutes from the estimate passed to ATC and the IP had to direct the timing and fly part of the inbound leg. Further study of the holding timing procedure in the Techniques and Procedures Manual is required.

SP, due to task sequencing that concentrated all cockpit workload inside the turn, left the pre-descent checks and the navigation aid setup for the outbound turn and did not maintain the holding radial while completing them. The deviation from the holding pattern reached 13 degrees and the aircraft approached the edge of the protected holding airspace, with the result that the IP directed the correction and flew part of the pattern. Distribution of the cockpit tasks along the straight legs is required.

SP, due to applying on the outbound leg the same drift correction read from the inbound leg without doubling it, did not compensate for the wind change reported at the holding altitude and allowed the pattern to widen downwind. The deviation was recognized with delay and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the result that the deviation from the holding pattern reached 8 degrees. Application of the standard outbound drift correction is required on every circuit.

SP, due to acceptance of the automated solution without an independent check of the parameters, flew the pattern from the GPS holding depiction without cross-checking the holding radial and the holding speed against the raw navigation picture. The airspeed error of 20 knots was identified only after the IP's verbal prompt and corrected with delay, with the result that the inbound leg was flown outside the holding speed for its full length. An independent raw-data check of the pattern parameters is required.

SP entered the holding pattern correctly, complied with the ATC holding clearance and compensated for the wind changes without the IP's intervention. However, the accuracy remained at the edge of the desired standard, with the deviation from the holding pattern twice reaching 6 degrees and the airspeed 14 knots off the holding speed before the self-correction took effect. Marginal performance for the Training Section - earlier recognition of the drift on the outbound leg is expected to improve.

SP determined the entry sector before the fix and established the aircraft on the holding radial immediately, flying the pattern accurately and quickly. Wind changes at the holding altitude were compensated without the IP's intervention, keeping the deviation from the holding pattern inside 3 degrees, the airspeed within 6 knots of the holding speed and the crossing of the IAF within 40 seconds of the estimate passed to ATC. Pre-descent checks were executed inside the pattern without prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the holding pattern with exceptional accuracy, selecting the entry before reaching the fix and cross-checking the GPS depiction against the raw radial and DME picture on every circuit. Drift correction was anticipatory, so that the deviation from the holding pattern remained within 1 degree, the airspeed within 3 knots of the holding speed and the crossing of the IAF within 10 seconds of the estimate. The aircraft remained well inside the protected holding airspace and every ATC instruction was read back and complied with as issued. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an unstandardized cross-check between the HSI and the leg timing during the holding turns, did not roll out on the holding radial and did not re-intercept it on the inbound leg. The error persisted over two circuits, with the result that the deviation from the holding pattern exceeded 11 degrees, the airspeed diverged by 25 knots from the holding speed and the IP directed the corrections and flew part of the inbound leg. Further study of the holding pattern cross-check sequence in the Techniques and Procedures Manual is required.

SP, due to attention captured by a minor system indication while the aircraft state went unmonitored, did not continue the holding pattern cross-check and did not start the outbound timing at the abeam position. The deviation from the holding pattern reached 12 degrees and the crossing of the IAF differed by 3 minutes from the estimate passed to ATC, with the result that the IP had to direct the recovery of the pattern and fly part of it. Maintaining the pattern cross-check while handling a secondary indication is required.

SP, due to a drift correction applied only after the deviation had appeared on the HSI instead of from the winds computed before entry, did not compensate for the wind change on the outbound leg and did not adjust the outbound timing accordingly. The deviations were identified and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the result that the deviation from the holding pattern reached 8 degrees and the crossing of the IAF differed by 2 minutes from the estimate. Anticipatory application of the drift correction is required on every circuit.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary cockpit task during a critical phase of flight, did not keep the holding speed in the cross-check while setting up the navigation aid and did not execute the pre-descent checks before the inbound leg. The airspeed error of 20 knots was recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompt, with the result that the inbound leg was flown outside the holding speed for its full length. Completion of the cockpit setup on the straight legs, with the airspeed retained in the cross-check, is required.

SP, due to a late start of the outbound timing after the wings-level point, did not produce a one minute inbound leg on the first circuit and adjusted the outbound leg only on the following circuit. The error was identified and corrected by the SP without the IP's intervention, with the result that the crossing of the IAF differed by 1.5 minutes from the estimate passed to ATC. Starting the outbound timing at the abeam position or at wings level, whichever occurs later, is expected on every circuit.

SP, due to complacency in a familiar pattern that replaced an active scan, reduced the frequency of the holding radial cross-check on the outbound leg and applied the drift correction later than the wind change required. The deviation was recognized by the SP and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention, with the result that the deviation from the holding pattern reached 7 degrees and the airspeed 13 knots off the holding speed before being brought back. A continuous cross-check of the pattern is expected on every circuit, including familiar holding fixes.

SP entered the holding pattern accurately and quickly, complied with the ATC holding clearance and compensated for the wind changes without the IP's intervention. However, performance was at the edge of the desired standard, with the deviation from the holding pattern twice reaching 5 degrees and the crossing of the IAF differing by 1 minute from the estimate passed to ATC. Marginal performance for the Training Section - a more immediate drift correction on the outbound leg is expected to improve.

SP flew the holding pattern to a standard above the level desired for this stage, determining the entry before reaching the fix and applying the drift correction anticipatorily on each leg. The deviation from the holding pattern remained within 2 degrees, the airspeed within 3 knots of the holding speed and the crossing of the IAF within 15 seconds of the estimate passed to ATC. Pre-descent checks were completed inside the pattern without prompting and the aircraft remained well within the protected holding airspace. Above end of block MIF achieved.
